text:
most companies will deploy AI employees backwards.

they’ll connect every app, upload every document, and ask the agent to do everything.

a better rollout:
- pick one workflow that happens 10+ times a week
- define exactly what “done” looks like
- give it 20 examples of good work
- require approval before external actions
- log every mistake and correction
- expand its role only after it becomes reliable

the goal is one boring job it can reliably take off the team’s plate.

text:
a lot of AI SaaS are about to die, for one simple reason: the tools never act for your business

they sit outside the work... they record the meeting, score the call, build the report, flag the risk, and hand all of it back to you to deal with

the next generation of agents lives where you already are: in your meetings and in the channels where your team talks

you hand one a task like you'd hand it to a coworker and it comes back done, it just gets work done

the listeners are getting replaced by teammates, and that's exactly what i like about this launch

here's an example of what i mean: i tagged @getlindy for last month's tool spend per client against what we invoiced... 15 minutes later the sheet was in the thread, two clients flagged as costing more to run than they pay
